Anchor B's own loss also exceeded 1 (a passivity violation on the raw unprojected eps_override channel, attributed not ignored), evidence the fitted anchor is not self-evidently more correct -- whether production should anchor on it is a separate, undecided design question

port_families.ad_evidence: f64 AD-vs-FD referee (scripts/diagnostics/msl_ad_band_mean_s21_owner_measurement.py, gpu-rtx4090, VESSL 369367251813/369367251827; tracked run log with both runs' full measurement tables and the actual pytest gate's PASS output -- the raw logs live only under the primary checkout's gitignored .omx/ -- is scripts/diagnostics/msl_ad_band_mean_owner_measurement/owner_runs_20260804.md): rel_err 0.0026 at num_periods=20 through the full extraction, on the gate's own fixture at its own h=1e-3, differentiating band-mean |S21|^2 (tests/_msl_ad_objective.py, shared with the #515 AD smoke) rather than the prior sum_ij|S_ij|^2 objective (issue #530 -- that objective was 99.96% a passivity-pinned structural constant, which is why it went blind after PR #516). A 5-point h-sweep over h in [3e-4, 1e-2] reads rel_err 0.0002-0.0146 with a 1.583% FD spread; the gate threshold 0.03 is derived from the sweep's worst point via tests._gate_policy.gate_from_envelope. A planted issue-#483-class defect (eps_override frozen before tracing, so the traced parameter never reaches the AD tape) reads rel_err 1.0000 on the same fixture -- the gate reds at 33x the threshold, the resolving-power falsifier issue #529 established as discipline. This supersedes the pre-#530 objective's rel_err 0.0331 against a 0.10 threshold (issue #527, closed; that run: VESSL 369367250775, gate's own measured run VESSL 369367250794) and the older pre-#516 0.000110 figure (issues #483/#486). The new objective is NOT immune to the same shape of failure an extractor fix could cause -- an extractor fix that shrinks |S11| would shrink this gradient too -- but MEASURED (not narrated): the level dropped 16x on this fixture (16.00599 to 0.99787211), cutting the loss's float32 ULP 32x and lifting f32 resolving power from 4.45 to 53.8 ULP at the gate's h, and the residue from unity (~2.5e-3, order |S11|^2 with |S11| ~ 0.05 here) is now a physical observable rather than a unitarity-violation artifact; that risk is CONTAINED -- by the f64 comparator's 2.9e6x resolving-power headroom above _MIN_FD_ULP_SPAN and by the resolving-power floor assert (issue #527's fix, unchanged by the objective swap) reporting a comparator failure loudly instead of silently -- not eliminated. What mechanism drives the gradient (a reference-plane artifact against the wave split's frozen Hammerstad-Jensen z0_hj, or genuine beta/reflection physics) is RESOLVED (issue #560, 2026-08-06; scripts/diagnostics/msl_ad_z0_anchor_probe.py, run log scripts/diagnostics/msl_ad_z0_anchor_probe_run_20260806.md): anchoring the wave split on a frozen per-port fitted z0 (measured at alpha=1, held constant) instead of the frozen analytic z0_hj and re-measuring g_ad on this same fixture (CPU/float32) collapsed |g_ad| from 1.602236e-03 (bit-identical across 2 repeats) to 6.885110e-05 (headline value from an un-repeated run, killed mid-way by a background-task duration limit; the bit-identical-2/2-confirmed value under a CLI-rounded anchor is 6.884444e-05, agreeing to 4 significant figures). Issue #560's own criterion is QUALITATIVE ('drops toward the FD-unresolvable floor'), not a numeric ratio: the estimated FD signal for this g_b at the gate's h is only ~1.16 ULP of a float32 loss, below the 4.449 ULP issue #527 measured for the retired objective's f32 comparator and declared untrustworthy -- g_b is noise-floor by this repo's own established standard, which settles the issue on its own terms. As a SECONDARY, self-declared check (NOT a quote from #560, whose body contains no numeric threshold -- an earlier draft of this evidence wrongly attributed '5x' to the issue as verbatim, corrected here), the ratio is ~23.3x, 4.6x past this PR's own pre-declared 5x bar. Either way, the reference-plane artifact (mechanism 2) is the dominant channel, not beta/reflection physics (mechanism 1); this is a channel-attribution finding and does not change the rel_err/threshold numbers above. Separately, anchor B's own loss exceeded 1 (a passivity violation, attributed to the raw unprojected eps_override channel per compute_msl_s_matrix's docstring, not a threat to the ratio-based attribution) -- evidence the fitted anchor is not self-evidently 'more correct', so whether compute_msl_s_matrix's PRODUCTION wave split should anchor on it is a SEPARATE, undecided design question this PR does not settle. Launch-fixture staticness is regression-locked by tests/test_msl_source_fixture_static.py (pre-fix 0.126 vs gate 0.03 at num_periods=1); smoke/end-to-end: tests/test_msl_sparam_ad.py (rebuilt alongside this gate, issue #515) and tests/test_sparam_ad_end_to_end.py.

port_families.validation_status: The one-port TEM-line reflection API has broad analytic validation over termination, impedance, frequency, and mesh axes plus a broad MEEP short/open comparison. (issue #489 stage 2) is a separate, two-drive through-line extension -- not covered by the 1-port evidence above -- whose own EXPERIMENTAL label was LIFTED 2026-08-06 (PI decision) to VALIDATED WITH SCOPE once its external-referee, mesh-refinement, wiring-pin, and AD legs all closed; see its own known_limits entry and tests/test_coax_two_port_fdtd.py. The power-wave cross-family normalization (per-port sqrt(Z0) division before the two-drive solve) is validated by planted-voltage unit tests under UNEQUAL port impedances, independent of any FDTD run. TWO committed FDTD fixtures. Attempt 1: trips its own reciprocity falsifier (94-100% deviation) -- root-caused (post-review) to the MSL probe ladder spanning only 0.34%-3.37% of the guided wavelength, too short for the matrix-pencil wave split (instrument scoping). Whether the junction's own physical reflection also contributed to that reciprocity miss was left UNRESOLVED by attempt 1 alone (root-causing the probe-ladder defect does not rule out a second, smaller contributor). Attempt 2 (PI-directed, R2 escape clause): lengthened the MSL ladder 1.0mm->8.0mm and widened the x-CPML clearance 200um->1500um, junction geometry byte-identical to attempt 1 (asserted). A RUN-LENGTH INVARIANCE TEST across two settling checkpoints (20000 -> 45000 steps) is the discriminator: the fitted gamma-vs-analytic-beta ratio is STABLE and in-band [0.8,1.3] at BOTH checkpoints. Reciprocity (0.824->0.938), |S22| (0.451->1.104), and max|S| (0.9933->1.1038, crossing the passivity-guard hard limit) all FAILED that same invariance test at those two checkpoints -- still evolving in the WRONG direction -- so at that point they were UNMEASURED AT THIS SETTLING, not 'refuted with cause identified'. A prior write-up of this result attributed the reciprocity miss to a coax/MSL drive-amplitude gap; this was RETRACTED after a second review found it mathematically impossible (per-drive column rescaling of the two-drive solve leaves S exactly invariant by construction) and found the invoked 'amplitude ratio' equal to raw cond_a under a new name -- the third retracted attribution on this lane. SETTLED RUN (VESSL 369367252283, 2026-08-06, n_steps=135000, same attempt-2 fixture unmodified): both drives clear the -40 dB ring-down rule for the first time on this lane (settling_db -45.94/-44.17 dB). gamma-vs-beta is now CONFIRMED (a third checkpoint, at full settling, still in-band [0.8,1.3]: 1.148/0.859/1.051). Passivity is ATTRIBUTED: settled max|S|=0.9933 with the strict passivity guard clean -- the earlier 1.1038/1.218 excursions are now understood as truncation artifacts of an unsettled run, not a real violation. Reciprocity is now MEASURED, not merely disclosed: worst deviation 91.4% (pair (0,1)) AT FULL SETTLING, explained by none of this lane's three retracted attributions -- reported as a real property of this fixture's own measurement (either genuine loss/coupling asymmetry or a surviving instrument limitation), deliberately NOT adjudicated.
